injuries.injury: Sharpe registered 15 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes in Sunday's 98-90 win over the Pacers.
injuries.detail: Sharpe dominated the glass, collecting four offensive rebounds while shooting efficiently en route to his first double-double of the season. It was also the second time he scored in double digits this season. Sharpe's rebounding provides a useful foundation, although his ceiling will depend on whether Brooklyn consistently gives him enough touches and playing time -- he has played more than 25 minutes just twice all season long.

injuries.injury: The Nets exercised Demin's third-year team option for the 2027-28 season, Sharif Phillips-Keaton of USA Today reports Thursday.
injuries.detail: Brooklyn's decision keeps Demin under contract through the 2027-28 campaign as the organization continues investing in its young backcourt. The move provides additional long-term stability but doesn't directly impact his immediate fantasy outlook. Demin is currently dealing with a right leg bone bruise and is scheduled to be re-evaluated in one week.

injuries.injury: Bilodeau (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
injuries.detail: Bilodeau will miss a third straight game to begin the regular season due to a right shoulder sprain. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

injuries.injury: Carter (illness) practiced with the G League's Maine Celtics on Wednesday.
injuries.detail: Carter is working back from mononucleosis, which has prevented him from making his season debut. A two-way player, Carter figures to begin his season in Maine as opposed to Boston once healthy.

injuries.injury: Smith (hand) won't return to Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
injuries.detail: Smith has been starting for Nic Claxton (hamstring), who hasn't played this season. However, the Bulls will be down another big, at least for the remainder of Wednesday's contest. As a result, Zach Collins should handle most of the minutes in the middle the rest of the way.

injuries.injury: Head coach Tiago Splittler said Friday that Claxton (hamstring) is expected to make his season debut Sunday against the 76ers, per Joel Lorenzi of The Athletic.
injuries.detail: Splitter stopped short of confirming Claxton's availability, but the big man is certainly trending in the right direction. Once Claxton is cleared to make his Bulls debut, Jalen Smith (hand) is likely to fall into a reserve role.

injuries.injury: Collins didn't practice Friday due to an illness, per K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network.
injuries.detail: Collins left Wednesday's loss to the Knicks early, presumably due to the ailment. For now, he can be tentatively labeled as questionable for Saturday's game versus the 76ers.

injuries.injury: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Monday's game against the Kings.
injuries.detail: Although there haven't been any negative reports regarding Lively's rehab progress, it doesn't appear he will be back in the lineup anytime soon. For now, the 22-year-old should be considered week-to-week. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford and Moussa Cisse should continue to handle most of the work at the five. Santi Aldama (knee) might also get involved in that area once he's cleared to return.

injuries.injury: De Larrea (knee) is out for Friday's game against Utah.
injuries.detail: De Larrea continues to miss time with a right knee strain, and it's not clear at this time where he's at in his rehab. He can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

injuries.injury: Biberovic (heel) is listed as out for Monday's game against Sacramento.
injuries.detail: Biberovic has been battling inflammation in his right heel, preventing him from making his NBA debut. While the rookie should be considered week-to-week, he likely has a way to go before earning a meaningful role in Dallas even when he's cleared to suit up.

injuries.injury: Joe (hip) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Philadelphia.
injuries.detail: Joe will miss Wednesday's contest due to a right hip contusion, resulting in his fifth straight absence. This will continue to open up additional minutes on the perimeter for Detroit's reserves. Joe's next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Lakers.

injuries.injury: Duren will be re-evaluated in two weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
injuries.detail: Duren suffered the hamstring injury in Friday's win over Miami and is set to miss an extended period. Paul Reed is expected to join the starting five and carries significant fantasy value until Duren returns. John Collins and Tolu Smith are also candidates to see a bump in minutes in Duren's stead.

injuries.injury: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
injuries.detail: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

injuries.injury: Ingram (Achilles) has progressed to full contact basketball activities, per NBA writer Justin Russo.
injuries.detail: Ingram told reporters Friday he's close to returning, though a concrete timeline for his season debut has yet to be disclosed. The star forward is recovery from a partial Achilles tear, and it sounds like he'll be ready to roll at some point in mid-November.

injuries.injury: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
injuries.detail: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

injuries.injury: The Clippers recalled Niederhauser (foot) from the G League's San Diego Clippers on Sunday.
injuries.detail: Niederhauser remains unlikely to play a meaningful role in the short term following a seven-month recovery from foot surgery. The 23-year-old might instead make a phased return to action, possibly seeing limited minutes at some point in upcoming weeks and making some appearances in the G League. Last season, he averaged 4.3 points, 2.9 rebounds and 0.3 assists per regular-season game during his rookie year.

injuries.injury: Jones (ankle/two-way player) is out for Friday's game against Toronto.
injuries.detail: It's not clear whether Jones is still dealing with a right ankle injury, or if he's been ruled out due to his status as a two-way player. He'll presumably open the year with the G League's Wisconsin Herd once he's back at full strength.

injuries.injury: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
injuries.detail: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

injuries.injury: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
injuries.detail: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

injuries.injury: Beringer was ruled out for the second half of Friday's game against the Pelicans due to a nasal fracture, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
injuries.detail: Although Beringer's nasal fracture will prevent him from returning to Friday's contest, he may be able to play through the injury during future games while wearing a mask. Trey Lyles stands to benefit from increased minutes in the meantime.

injuries.injury: Shannon (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
injuries.detail: Shannon's absence will leave Minnesota a bit shorthanded on the wing. His limited role makes the absence unlikely to have a significant fantasy impact, though the Timberwolves could distribute his available minutes among their remaining perimeter players.

injuries.injury: Missi (knee) is out for Friday's game against Minnesota.
injuries.detail: Missi has been sidelined since picking up his injury Oct. 23. He remains without a timetable to return.

injuries.injury: Bona (neck) is listed as out for Friday's game versus the Cavaliers.
injuries.detail: While Bona isn't starting Friday, his absence will open up minutes behind Joel Embiid. With Dominick Barlow (back) also sidelined against Cleveland, the 76ers should need more minutes out of Jabari Walker. Tacko Fall might also see action for the first time of the 2026-27 season.

injuries.injury: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.detail: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

injuries.injury: Head coach Nick Nurse said Wednesday that Barlow (back) likely needs another 10-12 days before he's cleared to return to the court, Derek Bodner of AllPHLY.com reports.
injuries.detail: Nurse added that the team is "pretty positive" that Barlow's back is getting better, though he's still going to have to wait some more time before being cleared. The big man has yet to make his season debut due to a lumbar spine bone stress response, and he isn't expected to return until mid-November at the earliest.

injuries.injury: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
injuries.detail: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

injuries.injury: Hunter (illness) is listed as out for Friday's game against San Antonio.
injuries.detail: Hunter was listed as questionable but has now been ruled out for the first time this season. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday versus the Heat. Without Hunter, Malik Monk might find his way into the starting lineup.

injuries.injury: Murray (ankle) will be re-evaluated in 10-to-14 days, NBA reporter Marc Stein reports.
injuries.detail: Murray has officially been diagnosed with left ankle capsulitis, and he's set to miss at least the next 10 days. Precious Achiuwa has been starting in Murray's absence, and he should continue to see opportunities along with De'Andre Hunter and Daeqwon Plowden.

injuries.injury: Raynaud (knee) is progressing in his rehabilitation and will be re-evaluated in approximately two weeks, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
injuries.detail: Raynaud's absence is expected to extend into mid-November due to a right patellar subluxation. With Dylan Cardwell (calf) set to miss at least one more week, Precious Achiuwa, Jonathan Mogbo and De'Andre Hunter are candidates for increased minutes in the frontcourt.

injuries.injury: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.detail: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

injuries.injury: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
injuries.detail: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

injuries.injury: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
injuries.detail: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.
